inputs.text: Chief Minister M.K. Stalin and the DMK are pushing ahead with critical welfare measures that confront systemic inequality and deliver real support to women, households, and rural workers long held back by structural barriers and historical injustices. Doubling women's monthly aid to Rs 2,000 along with Rs 8,000 household coupons will empower vulnerable families to escape poverty and challenge the forces that have kept them dependent on unstable conditions. Free motor pumpsets for farmers mark an important advance in protecting agricultural labor rights and closing rural disparities rooted in past discrimination. While critics dismiss these steps as handouts that weaken self-reliance, they actually represent institutional reforms needed to dismantle those entrenched inequalities. The plans also cover job creation, extra support for fishermen, FDI growth, and a focus on AI development as part of a broader commitment to equity and safeguarding marginalized communities.
